# Baruch Chapter 2 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Vaticanus, Baruch 2

---

**1** And the Lord our God has carried out the word he spoke against us, and against our judges who judged Israel, against our kings and rulers, and against the men of Israel and Judah —

**2** to bring upon us great disasters such as have never been done under the whole heaven, such as happened in Jerusalem, in accordance with what is written in the law of Moses:

**3** that one man would eat the flesh of his own son and the flesh of his own daughter.

**4** He gave them over to subjection under all the kingdoms around us, to be a reproach and a desolation among all the surrounding peoples, where the Lord has scattered them.

**5** They were brought low and not raised up, because we sinned against the Lord our God and did not listen to his voice.

**6** Righteousness belongs to the Lord our God, but to us and to our ancestors belongs open shame, as it is this day.

**7** All these disasters have come upon us that the Lord threatened against us.

**8** Yet we did not seek the face of the Lord, that each of us might turn from the thoughts of his wicked heart.

**9** And the Lord kept watch over the disasters and brought them upon us; for the Lord is righteous in all his works that he has commanded us;

**10** yet we did not obey his voice or walk in the commandments that the Lord set before us.

**11** And now, O Lord God of Israel, who brought your people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand, and with signs and wonders and great power and an outstretched arm, and made yourself a name as it is to this day —

**12** we have sinned, we have been ungodly, we have acted unjustly, O Lord our God, in defiance of all your ordinances.

**13** Let your wrath turn away from us, for we are left as a remnant among the nations where you have scattered us.

**14** Hear, O Lord, our prayer and our supplication; deliver us for your own sake and grant us favor in the sight of those who have taken us into exile,

**15** so that all the earth may know that you are the Lord our God, since Israel and his descendants are called by your name.

**16** Look down, O Lord, from your holy dwelling and take note of us; incline your ear, O Lord, and hear;

**17** open your eyes and look — for it is not the dead in Hades who will give glory and justification to the Lord,

**18** but the soul that is deeply grieved, who walks bent and weak, whose eyes are failing and whose soul is famished — it is that person who gives you glory and righteousness, O Lord.

**19** For it is not on account of the righteousness of our ancestors that we bring our supplication before you, O Lord our God,

**20** but because you have sent your wrath and anger upon us, just as you spoke through your servants the prophets, saying:

**21** "Thus says the Lord: Bow your shoulder and serve the king of Babylon, and remain in the land I gave to your ancestors.

**22** But if you do not obey the voice of the Lord by serving the king of Babylon,

**23** I will silence in the cities of Judah and in the streets around Jerusalem the voice of rejoicing and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, and the whole land will become a wasteland without inhabitant."

**24** But we did not listen to your voice, to serve the king of Babylon; and so you fulfilled the words you spoke through your servants the prophets, that the bones of our kings and the bones of our ancestors would be brought out from their places.

**25** And indeed they were thrown out to the scorching heat of the day and the bitter cold of the night, and they died in great misery by famine and sword and exile.

**26** And the house over which your name was called you have made as it is this day, because of the wickedness of the house of Israel and the house of Judah.

**27** Yet you have dealt with us, O Lord our God, according to all your goodness and according to all your great compassion,

**28** as you spoke through your servant Moses on the day you commanded him to write your law before the children of Israel, saying:

**29** "If you will not heed my voice, this great and numerous people will certainly dwindle among the nations where I will scatter them.

**30** For I know that they will not listen to me, because they are a stiff-necked people; but in the land of their exile they will have a change of heart,

**31** and they will know that I am the Lord their God. I will give them a heart and ears that hear,

**32** and they will praise me in the land of their exile and will remember my name,

**33** and they will turn from their stubbornness and from their evil deeds, for they will remember the way of their ancestors who sinned before the Lord.

**34** Then I will bring them back to the land that I swore to give to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, and they will possess it; and I will multiply them, and they will not be diminished.

**35** And I will make with them an everlasting covenant, to be their God and they shall be my people; and I will no longer remove my people Israel from the land I have given them."

---

## Council Notes

**On v.8 — "entreat the face" vs. "seek the face":** EMET "entreat the favor"; LOGOS "entreat the face" (literal); PNEUMA "seek the Lord's face." Consensus: "seek the face of the Lord" preserves the Semitic idiom without needing a gloss.

**On v.17 — "justification" alongside "glory":** All agents note the unusual pairing. Greek dikaiōsin may mean "vindication" or "righteousness." The paradox is that only the living griever, not the dead, can declare God righteous in his judgments. Retained as "glory and justification" in consensus.

**On v.18 — "soul that is grieved":** EMET "soul that is grieved over the greatness of evil"; LOGOS and PNEUMA simplify. Consensus condenses but retains the "grieved soul" as the subject — the most theologically significant image in the passage.

**On v.29 — "dwindle":** EMET "become small"; LOGOS "dwindle to a few"; PNEUMA "dwindle to nothing." Consensus: "dwindle" without further qualification, closest to Greek eis oligostous.

**On vv.21-23 — Jeremiah oracle:** All agents agree on close translation. The voice/silence contrast (laughter, gladness, bridegroom, bride) deserves its full force. Consensus retains all four pairs.
